name: Chess set
blurb: A full chess set. Pull it apart to sort the pieces by how they move.
credit: "A Beautiful Game" by the MaterialX Project (ASWF), glTF conversion by Ed Mackey, CC BY 4.0

Board.info: 64 squares in an 8 by 8 grid. Each player starts with a light square in the right-hand corner.

White king and queen.info: The king moves one square any way; lose him and you lose. The queen moves any distance in any straight line.

Black king and queen.info: Black's king and queen. The queen is the strongest piece, worth about nine pawns.

White pawns.info: Eight pawns move one square forward and capture diagonally. One that reaches the far side becomes a queen.

Black pawns.info: Black's eight pawns. On its first move a pawn may advance two squares instead of one.

White rooks.info: Rooks move any distance along a row or column, and join the king in castling.

Black rooks.info: Black's rooks, shaped like castle towers. Two rooks working together are worth more than a queen.

White knights.info: Knights move in an L shape, two squares then one to the side, and are the only pieces that jump.

Black knights.info: Black's knights. A knight always lands on a square of the opposite colour to where it started.

White bishops.info: Bishops move any distance diagonally, so each one stays on squares of a single colour all game.

Black bishops.info: Black's bishops: one on light squares, one on dark. Together they cover the whole board.
